Pilot/main-wave planning summary

Source: R/cmr_plan.R
pilot_plan.Rd

Summarize the pilot-size viability band, the smallest viable pilot, and the pilot size given by the two-thirds-power rule of the accompanying paper.

Usage

pilot_plan(
  n,
  sigma1,
  sigma0,
  alpha = 0.05,
  method = c("bounded", "bernoulli"),
  input = c("sd", "variance"),
  accounting = c("design_only", "pooled"),
  desired_pilot = NULL,
  strict_upper = FALSE
)

cmr_plan(
  n,
  sigma1,
  sigma0,
  alpha = 0.05,
  method = c("bounded", "bernoulli"),
  input = c("sd", "variance"),
  accounting = c("design_only", "pooled"),
  desired_pilot = NULL,
  strict_upper = FALSE
)

Arguments

n

Total experimental sample size across pilot and main wave.

sigma1

Treatment-arm standard deviation, or variance when input = "variance".

sigma0

Control-arm standard deviation, or variance when input = "variance".

alpha

Target error level.

method

Planning method, either "bounded" or "bernoulli".

input

Whether sigma1 and sigma0 are standard deviations ("sd") or variances ("variance").

accounting

"design_only" applies the break-even pilot-share cap; "pooled" ignores that cap.

desired_pilot

Optional user-proposed pilot size to classify.

strict_upper

If FALSE, the default, a pilot size equal to the design-only break-even cap is feasible, as in the viability band of the accompanying paper. If TRUE, feasible pilot sizes must be strictly below the cap.

Value

A list of class cmr_pilot_plan with the following entries.

band

The viability band from pilot_viability_band().

suggested_pilot

The smallest pilot size in the band, or 0 when the band is empty. This is the least costly pilot at which CMR can leave balance. It is a floor, not an optimal size.

default_two_thirds_power

The pilot size 2 * ceiling(n^(2/3) / 2) from the two-thirds-power rule.

two_thirds_status

Where default_two_thirds_power falls relative to the band, using the same labels as desired_status.

desired_pilot, desired_status

The user-proposed pilot size and its classification: "inside_viability_band", "below_activation_threshold", "above_break_even_cap", "outside_budget", "not_admissible_odd", or "no_pilot".

recommendation, caveat

Text summaries. The caveat records that the band is necessary rather than sufficient.

The object has a compact print() method.

See also

Other pilot planning: activation_threshold_bounded(), break_even_pilot_share(), pilot_viability_band(), print.cmr_pilot_plan()

Examples

cmr_plan(
  n = 3000,
  sigma1 = 0.18,
  sigma0 = 0.28,
  desired_pilot = 120
)
#> <cmr_pilot_plan>
#>   n: 3000
#>   method: bounded, accounting: design_only
#>   viability band: 72 to 134 (even sizes)
#>   suggested_pilot: 72
#>   default_two_thirds_power: 210 (above_break_even_cap)
#>   desired_pilot: 120 (inside_viability_band)
